transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. As we all know, the new event-ingestion service is scheduled to enter production next Monday. Before we get there, I need to run through our standard architecture sign-off checklist. I'd like to hear from backend engineering, infrastructure, customer success operations, and security — any blockers or required controls we need to address before I record the final design. Let's go through each area systematically. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker. While reviewing an unrelated consumer integration this morning, I confirmed that the existing Ledger event consumer cannot preserve ordering across active-active replication. Production compatibility requires active-passive replication plus an explicit per-aggregate ordering guardrail. I have not yet updated the architecture document, but this directly conflicts with the draft design's active-active replication proposal.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker from infrastructure. Ten minutes ago I confirmed from the current production load model that our shared cluster can support at most 48 partitions for this service without starving the checkout stream — not the 96 partitions in the draft design. I was still reconciling the capacity worksheet and hadn't posted the number yet, but this needs to be resolved before we finalize.

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker from customer success operations. During a contract review this afternoon, I found that our enterprise tenant Linden requires all event processing and storage to remain in the EU region. Linden is included in the proposed initial cohort, and I have not yet added the routing exception to the design ticket. This means the current design does not account for Linden's EU-only data residency requirement.

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker from security. During a separate token-hardening task today, my security scan found personal data in the event payloads. This means the service requires field-level encryption and a maximum 30-day retention period — the 30-day cap directly conflicts with the draft design's proposed 90-day event-retention period. I have not yet opened the security finding, but this needs to be resolved before we finalize the design.
